title: The hot trend in smartphones? Not buying a new one
主要内容: The smartphone industry is facing a global slowdown in sales, with International Data Corporation reporting a 6.6% year-on-year decline in shipment volumes for the first quarter of 2019. To counter this, companies are introducing new, high-priced foldable devices and 5G-enabled phones. Samsung, the world's largest smartphone maker, launched the Galaxy Fold, a nearly $2,000 foldable smartphone that faced early issues. Huawei also announced a foldable phone priced around $2,600. However, consumer feedback from London, Singapore, and Guangzhou was largely negative, with users finding foldable phones strange and bulky. Ben Wood of CCS Insight noted that smartphones have become too similar in design and functionality, with marginal gains slowing down. Despite efforts to promote 5G technology, consumers remain hesitant to upgrade unless their current devices are no longer functional. The article discusses the growing interest in 5G technology and its potential impact on the smartphone market. While the United States is leading in 5G development, countries like China and Japan are also racing to launch their own versions of the technology. However, widespread adoption of 5G is expected to take time due to the ongoing construction of global infrastructure. Despite this, there is enthusiasm among potential customers for 5G phones. A user in Guangzhou expressed interest in purchasing a 5G phone because it is considered "trendy" and offers a "better internet system" that enables activities like video streaming. Similarly, a user in London mentioned that 5G would make tasks such as social media use and streaming Netflix more convenient. The article highlights the increasing demand for 5G technology and its potential to transform user experiences.
